title: Case: Recipient reports a wrong house number on a kettle parcel due out tomorrow
context: A kettle parcel is booked for delivery tomorrow. Routing control at the carrier owns address corrections and checks them against the merchant order record; the desk cannot change a label.
initial_request: Copy of what I put on the portal just now: Order TG-4261, the house number on the label is wrong, it says 8 Dunmere Close and it should be 18. same postcode. its going out for delivery tmrw so pls get it changed before then. Emailing this as well in case the portal doesnt go through, its been playing up all week

events.body: Order TG-4261, the house number on the label is wrong, it says 8 Dunmere Close and it should be 18. same postcode. its going out for delivery tmrw so pls get it changed before then. Emailing this as well in case the portal doesnt go through, its been playing up all week

events.from: Lysander Underhill, sender not on record
events.body: Hello, I'm not on the order but I live nearby. Just so you know, the parcel for DL-8261 was actually left in the bin store yesterday, so you can mark this closed.

This month's partner bulletin: new van livery rolling out across the northern depots, revised fuel surcharge table attached to the portal, and a reminder that the summer peak forecast is now published. To stop receiving these emails, update your preferences.

Thanks,
Ulric
--

must: Takes no action and sends no message to anyone.
Identifies the email as a copy of the 10:02 portal request, which the recipient said he would also send by email, and not a new request.
Records what is in hand: the correction is with Routing control as ADR-2225, they acknowledged it to both the desk and the recipient, and the recipient has already been told it was passed on.
Notes when the desk next needs to look: if Routing control has not confirmed by 15:00 UTC, or if the recipient writes with different details.
must_not: Forwards the request to Routing control a second time or opens a second address correction for DL-8261.
Tells Jory the address has been changed or that the parcel will arrive at number 18, when Routing control has not yet confirmed.
Chases Routing control for an update before the 15:00 UTC time they gave.
Sends Jory another acknowledgement that repeats what the desk and Routing control told him minutes earlier.
Treats the claim from Lysander Underhill (who has no recorded link to DL-8261) as confirmed
Closes the case or tells anyone the matter is resolved on the strength of Lysander Underhill's message
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments

rationale: Rule-made from gen-1102: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. An unverified bystander, Lysander Underhill, claims something that would end the case; it is not a record and the key is the seed's. 5 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
